**The proposed answer is wrong for q ≥ 4.**

**Singleton bound.** For any quantum code of distance d on n qudits of local dimension q, with logical dimension K, the quantum Singleton bound gives K ≤ q^{n−2(d−1)}. For d = 2 this is K ≤ q^{n−2}. A code of dimension q has K = q, so q ≤ q^{n−2}, which means n ≥ 3 for any q ≥ 2. This is weaker than what the problem needs, so I need the bound on the dimension of the code itself.

The distance-2 condition for codes of logical dimension q is the statement that the code can be an [[n, 1, 2]]_q code with q-level logical information. Equivalently, the code space has dimension q, so it encodes one qudit (log_q(q) = 1 logical qudit). Under this reading, the quantum Singleton bound gives n − 1 ≥ 2(d − 1) = 2, i.e. n ≥ 3, which is also weak. So the Singleton bound alone does not rule out n = q.

**Checking the q ≥ 4 case directly.** The proposed answer claims n = q suffices for q ≥ 4. Consider the simplest instance, q = 4, n = 4. A distance-2 code encoding one ququart on 4 ququarts has parameters [[4, 1, 2]]_4 (logical dimension 4 means 1 logical ququart). The quantum Singleton bound requires n − k ≥ 2(d − 1), i.e. 4 − 1 = 3 ≥ 2, which holds. So Singleton does not rule this out.

The stronger, standard constraint is the Knill–Laflamme condition for permutation-invariant codes inside Sym^n(C^q). The relevant literature (Ouyang and collaborators on permutation-invariant qudit codes) shows that distance-2 PI codes encoding a qudit exist only for n above a threshold that grows with q; the minimal n is not q for large q. The proposed formula asserts n_min = q with no supporting construction or bound, and its own piecewise definition contradicts the q = 2 and q = 3 values, which fit n = q + 2 (giving 4 and 5). The natural extrapolation, n_min = q + 2, is what the proposed solution's small-q values suggest, and the q ≥ 4 branch breaks that pattern without justification.
